title: ¿Dónde está el baño?
desc: Asking for the bathroom in somebody else’s house
setting: You are at doña Carmen's house for the first time and you need the bathroom.

options.feedback: Con permiso is what you say stepping into somebody's house. Faultless.
Fine, but con permiso is the piece that is missing.

options.en: I am going to come in now.
options.feedback: True but strange. Announcing it is not the same as asking leave.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.en: Would you like a cold drink?

options.es: Sí, gracias. Y disculpe, ¿dónde está el baño?
options.en: Yes, thank you. And excuse me, where is the bathroom?
options.feedback: You took the drink and put a disculpe in front of the question. Both halves right.
You will get there, but you skipped both the drink and the disculpe.
Refusing a drink outright is colder than you mean it. Take the fresco.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: Al fondo, a la derecha. Cuidado con el escalón.
steps.en: At the back, on the right. Watch the step.

options.en: Thank you, doña. I will be right back.
options.feedback: Ya vengo is what people say leaving the room for a minute. Very natural.
It answers her but leaves the room without a word.
You are going four metres, not leaving the country.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: Aquí te dejo el fresco en la mesa.
steps.en: I will leave the drink here on the table for you.

options.es: Muy amable, doña. Se lo agradezco.
options.en: That is very kind, doña. I appreciate it.
options.feedback: Se lo agradezco is warm and correct with a señora you have just met.
Perfectly fine. A little thin for the trouble she went to.
It sounds like you are refusing after the fact. Take it and thank her.
